text:
"Your cores are ringing at our reference pitch, captain. Someone in Coda thinks well of you." The $personRank sounds almost warm.
OR
"We can hear you before we see you. You are in tune. Welcome."

"Comm open. Voice and pitch confirmed. Good to hear you, captain."
OR
"Ah, a friend of the chorus. Forgive the hum; we are mid-shift." Behind the $personRank a row of tuners sit with their eyes closed, holding one long note.

"Cantorate vessel. State your business and keep clear of our formation; your drive noise is fouling our tuning."
OR
"We are on a working patrol, captain. Please do not cross our line." The $personRank does not quite look at the camera; $heOrShe is listening to something you cannot hear.

"You are out of tune, captain, and the whole choir can hear it." The $personRank's voice is steady, but the hum behind $himOrHer has gone ragged.
OR
"No voice sings alone. If you take us, all of Vell will know your name."

"You are out of tune, captain." The $personRank closes the channel before you can answer.
OR
"All voices, on my pitch." The order is not meant for you, and the hum on the channel rises into a single note.
